scope.description: One confirmation, two kinds of requester. An earlier remote read from node 2 and a later leader-local read are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group; the leader's own broadcast for the local read confirms both, and the ready-to-read result of the local read plus the reply delivered to node 2 are measured.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
The remote read is registered and forwarded through the real follower path; the local read is issued through the leader peer and enters the same queue with node 1 as its source.
The harness uses the leader's ordinary broadcast for the local read and delivers that heartbeat to node 3 only; no other message is reordered.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

basis.prefix: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It registers a node-level pending read on node 2 and forwards it through the real follower path, so the leader queues the remote context first. It then registers a pending read on the leader itself and calls the leader peer's ReadIndex, which queues the local context behind the remote one and broadcasts heartbeats carrying that local context. The harness delivers the heartbeat addressed to node 3 back to the leader, collects the resulting messages, and records the context of the reply addressed to node 2. It feeds the leader's own accumulated ReadyToRead output to a pendingReadIndex registered for the local read and records whether that read completed, then delivers the reply to node 2, feeds node 2's ReadyToRead output and the same applied index to its registry, and records whether the remote read completed.
basis.requirement: A single confirmation that returns an earlier remote request and a later local request must give each requester a result tagged with its own SystemCtx, and both admitted reads must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
basis.responsibility: handleLeaderReadIndex queues both requests and broadcasts the local context, handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation builds the local ready-to-read result from each request's own context but builds the remote reply from the confirming heartbeat's context, and the two node-level registries consume those results. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only which requester is local.

comparisons.description: The reply delivered to the earlier remote requester must carry the context that requester admitted.
The leader's own admitted read should complete after the confirmed index is applied.
The earlier remote requester's admitted read should also complete after the same confirmed index is applied.

before.description: Tick-driven ReadIndex batching. Two follower-originated ReadIndex requests are queued at the real leader of a three-voter in-process group, one ordinary leader tick produces the confirmation heartbeat, and the earlier requester's reply and pending-read completion are measured; a second case queues one read and runs the same tick path.
assumptions: The voter group is three real in-process Raft Peer handlers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3}; node 1 is leader and each node uses a test-only in-memory ILogDB.
Both reads are registered through the real node-level pendingReadIndex and forwarded by the real follower ReadIndex path.
The only scheduling input is one leader tick; the harness does not choose which heartbeat is delivered first or reorder any message.
The single-read control uses the same setup, the same tick path and the same consumer, with one queued request instead of two.
excluded: No NodeHost, transport, persistence, restart or snapshot path is exercised.
No proposal or membership change is made while the reads are outstanding.
The run observes reply-context association and pending-read completion only; it does not attempt to establish a stale data value.

prefix.before: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. Node 2 and node 3 each register a node-level pending read under a generated context and forward it to the leader through the real follower path, so both requests sit in the leader's readIndex queue. The harness then calls Tick once on the leader and pumps it; the produced heartbeat addressed to node 3 carries the newest queued context. That heartbeat is delivered to node 3, whose echo is returned to the leader, and the leader's replies are collected. The reply addressed to node 2 is emitted with its response context and log index, delivered to node 2's real handler, and the resulting ReadyToRead plus that log index are fed to pendingReadIndex.addReady and pendingReadIndex.applied; the run records the batch index and whether the read completed. The control case repeats the setup with only node 2's read queued, ticks the leader once, delivers the heartbeat carrying that single context, and records the same reply and completion fields.
prefix.after: The harness launches three real Raft peers with bootstrap membership {1,2,3} and ticks node 1 until its current-term no-op is committed. It registers a node-level pending read on node 2 and forwards it through the real follower path, so the leader queues the remote context first. It then registers a pending read on the leader itself and calls the leader peer's ReadIndex, which queues the local context behind the remote one and broadcasts heartbeats carrying that local context. The harness delivers the heartbeat addressed to node 3 back to the leader, collects the resulting messages, and records the context of the reply addressed to node 2. It feeds the leader's own accumulated ReadyToRead output to a pendingReadIndex registered for the local read and records whether that read completed, then delivers the reply to node 2, feeds node 2's ReadyToRead output and the same applied index to its registry, and records whether the remote read completed.

requirement.before: A leader-produced confirmation heartbeat must not cause an earlier queued ReadIndex request to be answered with a different request's SystemCtx, and the earlier requester's admitted read must complete once the confirmed index is applied.
requirement.after: A single confirmation that returns an earlier remote request and a later local request must give each requester a result tagged with its own SystemCtx, and both admitted reads must complete once the confirmed index is applied.

responsibility.before: leaderTick and broadcastHeartbeatMessage choose the context carried by the periodic heartbeat, handleLeaderHeartbeatResp feeds the echoed hint to handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation, and that handler builds each remote reply; the requesting node's pendingReadIndex consumes it. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only how many reads are queued before the tick.
responsibility.after: handleLeaderReadIndex queues both requests and broadcasts the local context, handleReadIndexLeaderConfirmation builds the local ready-to-read result from each request's own context but builds the remote reply from the confirming heartbeat's context, and the two node-level registries consume those results. The experiment exercises those real handlers and changes only which requester is local.

before.description: When a leader tick confirms the newest of two queued reads, the reply delivered to the earlier requester must still carry the context that requester admitted.
After the confirmed index is applied, the earlier requester's admitted read should complete.
With one queued read, the tick-driven reply must carry that read's own context.
With one queued read, the same tick-driven path should complete it.

after.description: The reply delivered to the earlier remote requester must carry the context that requester admitted.
The leader's own admitted read should complete after the confirmed index is applied.
The earlier remote requester's admitted read should also complete after the same confirmed index is applied.

revision_reason: Add a local-versus-remote case on a single confirmation to show which reply branch strands the earlier request.
